transcript.text: We had a power cut last night and now our Candy washer dryer is completely dead - no lights, nothing. Everything else in the house came back on. The plug fuse is fine, I swapped it. Help!

The next most likely culprit is a fault in the mains lead or the connection at the socket. Please try plugging the washer-dryer into a different, known-working socket in another room and attempt to switch it on; this will tell us if the machine has internal power loss or if the original circuit is faulty.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I've already tested the socket with a lamp and it works fine, so the socket isn't the problem. The machine is still dead. Do you want me to try a different room anyway?

No need to try a different room since we know the socket works. Since the machine is completely dead despite good power at the plug and socket, the issue is likely an internal break in the mains lead (often where it enters the cabinet) or a failure of the main PCB.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
The cable and plug look fine from the outside, no damage. I'm not going to take any panels off or touch the internals though. Is there anything else I can check, or is it an engineer job?

Plug fuse, and external cable are fine, this points to an internal break in the mains wiring (often where it enters the cabinet) or a failure of the main PCB caused by the power cut surge. This is an engineer job; please contact a qualified repair technician to inspect the internal connections and replace the faulty component.
